page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-192 is a graphics-optimized server instance designed for workloads requiring significant parallel processing capabilities. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 720.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes four integrated NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs to accelerate graphics rendering and parallel computing tasks.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage options. It also does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without resource contention from other tenants on the host system.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-192 represents a high-density resource profile where the cost is driven by the combination of a high vCPU count, substantial system memory, and multiple professional-grade GPUs. This configuration is tailored for specialized workloads such as large-scale 3D rendering, video encoding, machine learning inference, and complex simulation tasks that can leverage multiple GPUs alongside a high-core-count host processor.
